############################################################
# 01_data_QC.R
#
# Purpose:
#   Prepare RNA-seq count data for differential expression
#   analysis and perform sample-level quality control.
#
# Main steps:
#   1. Load count matrix and sample metadata
#   2. Map Ensembl IDs to gene symbols
#   3. Check sample matching
#   4. Create edgeR DGEList
#   5. Filter lowly expressed genes
#   6. Calculate TMM normalization factors
#   7. Calculate CPM and logCPM values
#   8. Generate QC plots
#   9. Generate VST data for additional QC
#  10. Save processed objects and session information
############################################################



# ==========================================================
# 1. USER SETTINGS
# ==========================================================

# ----------------------------------------------------------
# Project directory
# ----------------------------------------------------------

# CHANGE THIS to the main directory of your own project.
project_dir <- "YOUR/PROJECT/DIRECTORY/HERE"

# Input files
count_matrix_file <- "countmtx.csv"
metadata_file     <- "target.csv"

# Separator used in the metadata file.
# Common choices:
#   ","  for comma-separated CSV
#   ";"  for semicolon-separated CSV
metadata_separator <- ";"


# ----------------------------------------------------------
# Experimental-condition column
# ----------------------------------------------------------

# Name of the metadata column containing the experimental
# groups/conditions used later for differential expression.
condition_column <- "Condition"


# ----------------------------------------------------------
# Gene annotation
# ----------------------------------------------------------

# This script assumes mouse RNA-seq data and therefore uses
# org.Mm.eg.db.
#
# Set to FALSE if the count matrix already contains gene
# symbols instead of Ensembl IDs.
map_ensembl_to_symbol <- TRUE


# Ensembl IDs sometimes contain version numbers such as:
#
# ENSMUSG00000000001.5
#
# Set TRUE to remove ".5" before annotation.
strip_ensembl_version <- FALSE


# How should multiple Ensembl IDs mapping to the same
# gene symbol be handled?
#
# Options:
#   "first" = keep first occurrence
#             (reproduces the original workflow)
#
#   "sum"   = sum counts for duplicated gene symbols
#
#   "error" = stop if duplicate symbols are encountered
duplicate_symbol_action <- "first"


# ----------------------------------------------------------
# LOW-EXPRESSION FILTERING
# ----------------------------------------------------------

# Choose the filtering strategy.
#
# OPTION 1: manual CPM threshold
# Reproduces the original analysis:
#
#   retain genes with CPM > 1 in at least 2 samples
#
filter_method <- "manual_CPM"

cpm_cutoff  <- 1
min_samples <- 2


# Alternative examples:
#
# Less stringent:
# cpm_cutoff  <- 0.5
# min_samples <- 2
#
# More stringent:
# cpm_cutoff  <- 1
# min_samples <- 3
#
# Or use edgeR's filterByExpr:
# filter_method <- "filterByExpr"


# ----------------------------------------------------------
# Normalization
# ----------------------------------------------------------

# TMM = trimmed mean of M-values
normalization_method <- "TMM"


# ----------------------------------------------------------
# QC options
# ----------------------------------------------------------

# Run DESeq2 VST in addition to logCPM-based QC?
run_vst_qc <- TRUE

# Run additional PCA diagnostics such as scree/loadings plots?
run_extended_pca_qc <- TRUE


# ==========================================================
# 2. LOAD PACKAGES
# ==========================================================

library(edgeR)
library(DESeq2)
library(PCAtools)
library(org.Mm.eg.db)
library(AnnotationDbi)

library(ggplot2)
library(pheatmap)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(dplyr)


# ==========================================================
# 3. DEFINE PATHS AND OUTPUT FOLDERS
# ==========================================================

if (!dir.exists(project_dir)) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "Project directory does not exist:\n",
      project_dir,
      "\n\nPlease update 'project_dir' in USER SETTINGS."
    )
  )
}


count_matrix_path <- file.path(
  project_dir,
  count_matrix_file
)

metadata_path <- file.path(
  project_dir,
  metadata_file
)

qc_dir <- file.path(
  project_dir,
  "Results",
  "QC"
)

dir.create(
  qc_dir,
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)


# ==========================================================
# 4. CHECK INPUT FILES
# ==========================================================

if (!file.exists(count_matrix_path)) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "Count matrix not found:\n",
      count_matrix_path
    )
  )
}


if (!file.exists(metadata_path)) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "Metadata file not found:\n",
      metadata_path
    )
  )
}


# ==========================================================
# 5. LOAD COUNT MATRIX
# ==========================================================

countmtx <- read.csv(
  count_matrix_path,
  row.names = 1,
  check.names = FALSE
)


message(
  "Count matrix loaded: ",
  nrow(countmtx),
  " genes × ",
  ncol(countmtx),
  " samples."
)


# ----------------------------------------------------------
# Basic count-matrix checks
# ----------------------------------------------------------

if (anyNA(countmtx)) {
  stop(
    "Missing values were detected in the count matrix."
  )
}


if (!all(vapply(countmtx, is.numeric, logical(1)))) {
  stop(
    "One or more count-matrix columns are not numeric."
  )
}


if (any(as.matrix(countmtx) < 0)) {
  stop(
    "Negative counts were detected."
  )
}


if (anyDuplicated(colnames(countmtx)) > 0) {
  stop(
    "Duplicate sample names were detected in the count matrix."
  )
}


if (anyDuplicated(rownames(countmtx)) > 0) {
  warning(
    "Duplicate gene identifiers are present before annotation."
  )
}


# ==========================================================
# 6. MAP ENSEMBL IDS TO GENE SYMBOLS
# ==========================================================

if (map_ensembl_to_symbol) {

  ensembl_ids <- rownames(countmtx)


  # Optional removal of Ensembl version suffix
  if (strip_ensembl_version) {

    ensembl_ids <- sub(
      "\\..*$",
      "",
      ensembl_ids
    )
  }


  gene_symbols <- mapIds(
    org.Mm.eg.db,
    keys = ensembl_ids,
    keytype = "ENSEMBL",
    column = "SYMBOL",
    multiVals = "first"
  )


  # Number of genes without gene-symbol annotation
  n_unmapped <- sum(is.na(gene_symbols))

  message(
    "Genes without mapped gene symbols: ",
    n_unmapped
  )


  # Remove unmapped genes
  mapped <- !is.na(gene_symbols)

  countmtx <- countmtx[mapped, , drop = FALSE]
  gene_symbols <- gene_symbols[mapped]


  # --------------------------------------------------------
  # Handle duplicated gene symbols
  # --------------------------------------------------------

  n_duplicate_symbols <- sum(
    duplicated(gene_symbols)
  )

  message(
    "Duplicated gene-symbol mappings: ",
    n_duplicate_symbols
  )


  if (
    duplicate_symbol_action == "first"
  ) {

    # Reproduces the original workflow:
    # retain only the first occurrence.
    keep_unique <- !duplicated(gene_symbols)

    countmtx <- countmtx[
      keep_unique,
      ,
      drop = FALSE
    ]

    gene_symbols <- gene_symbols[
      keep_unique
    ]

    rownames(countmtx) <- gene_symbols

  } else if (
    duplicate_symbol_action == "sum"
  ) {

    # Sum counts for Ensembl IDs mapping to the same symbol.
    countmtx <- rowsum(
      as.matrix(countmtx),
      group = gene_symbols,
      reorder = FALSE
    )

    countmtx <- as.data.frame(
      countmtx,
      check.names = FALSE
    )

  } else if (
    duplicate_symbol_action == "error"
  ) {

    if (anyDuplicated(gene_symbols) > 0) {

      stop(
        paste0(
          "Duplicate gene symbols detected.\n",
          "Choose duplicate_symbol_action = 'first' or 'sum'."
        )
      )
    }

    rownames(countmtx) <- gene_symbols

  } else {

    stop(
      paste0(
        "Unknown duplicate_symbol_action: ",
        duplicate_symbol_action
      )
    )
  }
}


# Save annotated count matrix
write.csv(
  countmtx,
  file.path(
    project_dir,
    "countmtx_genesymbols.csv"
  ),
  row.names = TRUE
)


message(
  "Count matrix after annotation: ",
  nrow(countmtx),
  " genes."
)


# ==========================================================
# 7. LOAD SAMPLE METADATA
# ==========================================================

target <- read.csv(
  metadata_path,
  row.names = 1,
  sep = metadata_separator,
  check.names = FALSE
)


# Convert unusual characters in column names if necessary
names(target) <- iconv(
  names(target),
  to = "ASCII",
  sub = ""
)


# Check experimental-condition column
if (!(condition_column %in% colnames(target))) {

  stop(
    paste0(
      "The metadata column '",
      condition_column,
      "' was not found.\n\nAvailable columns:\n",
      paste(
        colnames(target),
        collapse = ", "
      )
    )
  )
}


# Convert condition to factor
target[[condition_column]] <- factor(
  target[[condition_column]]
)


message(
  "Experimental conditions: ",
  paste(
    levels(target[[condition_column]]),
    collapse = ", "
  )
)


# ==========================================================
# 8. CHECK SAMPLE MATCHING
# ==========================================================

count_samples <- colnames(countmtx)
metadata_samples <- rownames(target)


# Samples present in counts but absent from metadata
missing_metadata <- setdiff(
  count_samples,
  metadata_samples
)


# Samples present in metadata but absent from counts
missing_counts <- setdiff(
  metadata_samples,
  count_samples
)


if (length(missing_metadata) > 0) {

  stop(
    paste0(
      "These count-matrix samples are missing from metadata:\n",
      paste(
        missing_metadata,
        collapse = ", "
      )
    )
  )
}


if (length(missing_counts) > 0) {

  stop(
    paste0(
      "These metadata samples are missing from count matrix:\n",
      paste(
        missing_counts,
        collapse = ", "
      )
    )
  )
}


# Reorder metadata to exactly match the count-matrix columns.
#
# IMPORTANT:
# We reorder here rather than simply overwriting the metadata
# row names, because overwriting could accidentally assign
# the wrong metadata to samples.
target <- target[
  count_samples,
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]


# Final identity check
if (!identical(
  colnames(countmtx),
  rownames(target)
)) {

  stop(
    "Sample order could not be matched between counts and metadata."
  )
}


message(
  "Count matrix and metadata samples match correctly."
)


# ==========================================================
# 9. CREATE edgeR DGEList
# ==========================================================

count_matrix <- as.matrix(countmtx)

storage.mode(count_matrix) <- "numeric"


dge <- DGEList(
  counts = count_matrix,
  samples = target
)


# Save raw DGE object
saveRDS(
  dge,
  file.path(
    project_dir,
    "dge.rds"
  )
)


# ==========================================================
# 10. FILTER LOWLY EXPRESSED GENES
# ==========================================================

if (filter_method == "manual_CPM") {

  # --------------------------------------------------------
  # Manual CPM filtering
  #
  # Example:
  # cpm_cutoff  = 1
  # min_samples = 2
  #
  # means:
  # retain genes with >1 CPM in at least two samples.
  # --------------------------------------------------------

  keep <- rowSums(
    cpm(dge) > cpm_cutoff
  ) >= min_samples


} else if (
  filter_method == "filterByExpr"
) {

  # edgeR determines an appropriate expression filter based
  # on group structure and library sizes.

  keep <- filterByExpr(
    dge,
    group = target[[condition_column]]
  )


} else {

  stop(
    paste0(
      "Unknown filter_method: ",
      filter_method
    )
  )
}


message(
  "Genes before expression filtering: ",
  nrow(dge)
)

message(
  "Genes retained after expression filtering: ",
  sum(keep)
)

message(
  "Genes removed: ",
  sum(!keep)
)


if (sum(keep) == 0) {

  stop(
    "No genes passed the expression filter. Check your cutoff settings."
  )
}


dge_fil <- dge[
  keep,
  ,
  keep.lib.sizes = FALSE
]


# ==========================================================
# 11. TMM NORMALIZATION
# ==========================================================

dge_fil <- calcNormFactors(
  dge_fil,
  method = normalization_method
)


message(
  "Normalization method: ",
  normalization_method
)


# Save filtered/normalized edgeR object
saveRDS(
  dge_fil,
  file.path(
    project_dir,
    "dge_fil.rds"
  )
)


# ==========================================================
# 12. CALCULATE CPM AND logCPM
# ==========================================================

counts_per_million <- cpm(
  dge_fil
)

logCPMcounts <- cpm(
  dge_fil,
  log = TRUE
)


write.csv(
  counts_per_million,
  file.path(
    project_dir,
    "CPMs.csv"
  )
)


write.csv(
  logCPMcounts,
  file.path(
    project_dir,
    "logCPMs.csv"
  )
)


# ==========================================================
# 13. QC SUMMARY TABLE
# ==========================================================

qc_summary <- data.frame(
  Sample = colnames(dge$counts),

  Condition =
    target[
      colnames(dge$counts),
      condition_column
    ],

  Raw_library_size =
    colSums(dge$counts),

  Filtered_library_size =
    colSums(dge_fil$counts),

  TMM_norm_factor =
    dge_fil$samples$norm.factors,

  Expressed_genes_raw =
    colSums(dge$counts > 0),

  Expressed_genes_filtered =
    colSums(dge_fil$counts > 0)
)


write.csv(
  qc_summary,
  file.path(
    qc_dir,
    "QC_summary_per_sample.csv"
  ),
  row.names = FALSE
)


print(qc_summary)


# ==========================================================
# 14. QC PLOT: RAW COUNT DISTRIBUTIONS
# ==========================================================

pdf(
  file.path(
    qc_dir,
    "raw_counts.pdf"
  ),
  width = 10,
  height = 6
)


boxplot(
  dge$counts,
  xlab = "",
  ylab = "Raw counts",
  las = 2,
  main = "Distribution of raw counts"
)


dev.off()


# ==========================================================
# 15. QC PLOT: LIBRARY SIZES
# ==========================================================

library_size_df <- data.frame(
  Sample = colnames(dge$counts),
  Library_size = colSums(dge$counts)
)


p_library <- ggplot(
  library_size_df,
  aes(
    x = Sample,
    y = Library_size
  )
) +
  geom_col() +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(
    title = "Library sizes",
    x = "Sample",
    y = "Total raw read count"
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 1
    )
  )


ggsave(
  filename = file.path(
    qc_dir,
    "library_sizes.pdf"
  ),
  plot = p_library,
  width = 8,
  height = 5
)


# ==========================================================
# 16. QC PLOT: NUMBER OF EXPRESSED GENES
# ==========================================================

expressed_genes_df <- data.frame(
  Sample = colnames(count_matrix),
  Genes = colSums(count_matrix > 0)
)


p_genes <- ggplot(
  expressed_genes_df,
  aes(
    x = Sample,
    y = Genes
  )
) +
  geom_col() +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(
    title = "Number of genes with count > 0",
    x = "Sample",
    y = "Number of expressed genes"
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 90,
      hjust = 1
    )
  )


ggsave(
  filename = file.path(
    qc_dir,
    "expressed_genes.pdf"
  ),
  plot = p_genes,
  width = 8,
  height = 5
)


# ==========================================================
# 17. QC PLOT: NORMALIZED logCPM DISTRIBUTIONS
# ==========================================================

pdf(
  file.path(
    qc_dir,
    "normalized_logCPM.pdf"
  ),
  width = 10,
  height = 6
)


boxplot(
  logCPMcounts,
  xlab = "",
  ylab = "log2 counts per million",
  las = 2,
  main = "Distribution of normalized logCPM values"
)


dev.off()


# ==========================================================
# 18. CREATE VST DATA FOR ADDITIONAL QC
# ==========================================================

if (run_vst_qc) {

  # --------------------------------------------------------
  # IMPORTANT:
  #
  # The original script contained:
  #
  # keep_dds <- rowSums(counts(ddsfil,
  #                            normalized=TRUE) > 1)
  # ddsfil <- ddsfil[keep_dds, ]
  #
  # That produced numeric indices rather than a TRUE/FALSE
  # filter.
  #
  # In this clean version, we instead use the same genes
  # already selected by the edgeR expression filter.
  # --------------------------------------------------------


  vst_counts <- dge_fil$counts


  dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
    countData = vst_counts,
    colData = target,
    design = as.formula(
      paste0(
        "~ ",
        condition_column
      )
    )
  )


  dds <- estimateSizeFactors(
    dds
  )


  vstdds <- vst(
    dds,
    blind = TRUE
  )


  vst_matrix <- assay(
    vstdds
  )


  write.csv(
    vst_matrix,
    file.path(
      project_dir,
      "VST_counts.csv"
    )
  )


  # ========================================================
  # 19. SAMPLE-TO-SAMPLE DISTANCE HEATMAP
  # ========================================================

  sample_distances <- dist(
    t(vst_matrix)
  )


  sample_distance_matrix <- as.matrix(
    sample_distances
  )


  annotation_col <- data.frame(
    Condition = target[[condition_column]]
  )

  rownames(annotation_col) <- rownames(target)


  pdf(
    file.path(
      qc_dir,
      "sample_distance_heatmap.pdf"
    ),
    width = 8,
    height = 7
  )


  pheatmap(
    sample_distance_matrix,
    clustering_distance_rows = sample_distances,
    clustering_distance_cols = sample_distances,
    annotation_col = annotation_col,
    annotation_row = annotation_col,
    fontsize = 8,
    main = "Sample-to-sample distances"
  )


  dev.off()
}


# ==========================================================
# 20. PCA USING logCPM VALUES
# ==========================================================

pca_logCPM <- pca(
  logCPMcounts,
  metadata = dge_fil$samples
)


pdf(
  file.path(
    qc_dir,
    "PCA_logCPM.pdf"
  ),
  width = 7,
  height = 6
)


print(
  biplot(
    pca_logCPM,
    lab = pca_logCPM$metadata$Sample,
    colby = condition_column,
    legendPosition = "right",
    title = "PCA: logCPM"
  )
)


print(
  biplot(
    pca_logCPM,
    lab = NULL,
    colby = "lib.size",
    legendPosition = "right",
    title = "PCA: library size"
  )
)


dev.off()


# ==========================================================
# 21. PCA USING VST VALUES
# ==========================================================

if (run_vst_qc) {

  pca_vst <- pca(
    vst_matrix,
    metadata = target
  )


  pdf(
    file.path(
      qc_dir,
      "PCA_VST.pdf"
    ),
    width = 7,
    height = 6
  )


  print(
    biplot(
      pca_vst,
      lab = rownames(target),
      colby = condition_column,
      legendPosition = "right",
      title = "PCA: VST"
    )
  )


  dev.off()
}


# ==========================================================
# 22. OPTIONAL EXTENDED PCA QC
# ==========================================================

if (run_extended_pca_qc) {

  # Horn's parallel analysis
  horn <- parallelPCA(
    logCPMcounts
  )


  # Elbow method
  elbow <- findElbowPoint(
    pca_logCPM$variance
  )


  message(
    "Horn's method suggests ",
    horn$n,
    " principal components."
  )


  message(
    "Elbow method suggests approximately PC ",
    elbow,
    "."
  )


  # --------------------------------------------------------
  # Scree plot
  # --------------------------------------------------------

  pdf(
    file.path(
      qc_dir,
      "PCA_screeplot.pdf"
    ),
    width = 7,
    height = 5
  )


  print(
    screeplot(
      pca_logCPM,
      components = getComponents(
        pca_logCPM,
        1:min(
          20,
          ncol(logCPMcounts)
        )
      ),
      vline = c(
        horn$n,
        elbow
      )
    )
  )


  dev.off()


  # --------------------------------------------------------
  # Genes contributing most strongly to PCs
  # --------------------------------------------------------

  pdf(
    file.path(
      qc_dir,
      "PCA_loadings.pdf"
    ),
    width = 9,
    height = 7
  )


  print(
    plotloadings(
      pca_logCPM,
      rangeRetain = 0.01,
      labSize = 3,
      title = "PCA loadings",
      caption = "Top/bottom 1% of loadings",
      drawConnectors = TRUE
    )
  )


  dev.off()
}


# ==========================================================
# 23. FINAL SUMMARY
# ==========================================================

message(
  "QC processing completed successfully."
)

message(
  "Original number of genes: ",
  nrow(dge)
)

message(
  "Genes retained for downstream analysis: ",
  nrow(dge_fil)
)

message(
  "Number of samples: ",
  ncol(dge_fil)
)

message(
  "Filtering method: ",
  filter_method
)


if (filter_method == "manual_CPM") {

  message(
    "Filtering criterion: CPM > ",
    cpm_cutoff,
    " in at least ",
    min_samples,
    " samples."
  )
}


message(
  "QC results saved to:\n",
  qc_dir
)


# ==========================================================
# 24. SAVE SESSION INFORMATION
# ==========================================================

capture.output(
  sessionInfo(),
  file = file.path(
    project_dir,
    "sessionInfo_01_data_QC.txt"
  )
)
